messages:
amy_cs: :rotating_light: Customer Acme reports repeated 502/504s when hitting hosted inference endpoint api.redwood.ai/v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. They see timeouts at p95 and a spike of 5xxs. attaching sample request/trace id: trace=acme-7f9f

mike_sre: on it. can you paste a sample curl and any request ids?

amy_cs: curl attached:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-7b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```
Trace ids: acme-7f9f, acme-8011. customer says started ~09:12 and is still happening. they see 504 after ~15s.

opsbot: [ALERT] Hosted-gateway queue latency > 2s, 5xx rate up 8% (09:15 UTC)

mike_sre: seeing elevated 504s from edge -> runtime proxy timeouts. reproducer: sending bursts of 50 concurrent short requests causes queue depth to spike. logs show proxy upstream read timeout at ~15s.

raja_runtime: do we have any recent deploys to gateway or proxy in last hour? config changes?

grace_eng: no deploys to runtime in last 2 hrs. there was an autoscaler config tweak for dedicated pools but not hosted.

dave_oncall: rolling back keepalive tweak? edge pool shows many idle connections closed -> reconnect churn, increasing cold-starts. can we temporarily increase keepalive and open connections to reduce reconnects?

mike_sre: quick mitigations to try: 1) raise proxy read timeout to 30s for the path 2) bump upstream keepalive on edge pools 3) enable 503->fast-fail fallback for heavy tenants 4) enable limited burst queueing. I'll start 1 and 2 now.

raja_runtime: logging: please capture one full request lifecycle (edge id, proxy id, runtime pod id, kv-cache hit/miss flag). also capture the generation latency and kernel time.

amy_cs: sent full customer timeline and example logs (S3 link) including response headers: `x-rw-trace: acme-7f9f`, `x-upstream: proxy-12`

mike_sre: increased proxy read timeout to 30s on the route (09:22). bumping keepalive on ap-northeast pool from 60s -> 5m. monitoring now.

opsbot: [METRIC] 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 3% within 2m of timeout bump (09:24 UTC). p95 latency still elevated vs baseline.

raja_runtime: good. but need root cause: why did the queue blow up? any misuse from tenant (thundering bursts) or KV cache evictions?

grace_eng: telemetry shows a burst correlated to a batch ingest job from Acme at 09:11 that opened many concurrent short-lived sessions (no streaming). KV-cache warmup rate high; eviction spikes at 09:10-09:12.

dave_oncall: action: ask CS to request the customer to stagger requests while we stabilize. amy_cs please coordinate.

amy_cs: told customer to throttle to <10 concurrent and they acknowledged. meanwhile customer asks for timeline and mitigation steps.

mike_sre: follow-ups (short): - add temporary route-level circuit breaker to reject at 200 concurrent - enable early-fallback to smaller model (gpt-open-3b) on 75% queue threshold - add burst backpressure that queues on runtime not gateway

raja_runtime: follow-ups (medium): - add enhanced tracing for proxy->runtime handoff including KV cache hits/misses - investigate KV cache eviction policy; consider more aggressive warmup for high-tenancy customers - review connection pool tuning and keepalive defaults

grace_eng: follow-ups (long): - postmortem with customer timeline, instrumentation gaps, and SLA impact - rollout automated warmup for top 10 tenants during peak windows - create runbook steps for oncall to increase keepalive and timeouts safely

amy_cs: immediate owner assignments: mike_sre (mitigation/timeout bump + circuit breaker), raja_runtime (tracing + cache investigation), grace_eng (postmortem and customer comms), dave_oncall (oncall playbook updates). I'll email the customer summary after we confirm stability.

mike_sre: confirmed stable for now, 5xx down to 1.2% and customer reports fewer errors. will keep monitoring for 2h.

opsbot: [INCIDENT] incident-tag: hosted-fanout-502s-9876543212 created, severity=P2, owners=[mike_sre, raja_runtime], runbook=temporary-protect-burst

dave_oncall: scheduled follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. invite: eng-runtime, eng-sre, cs, and product.

amy_cs: thanks all. customer is satisfied with immediate steps. will provide timeline + request for support credit if SLA threshold crossed.

raja_runtime: note for postmortem: instrument `x-kv-hit` header at proxy so CS can correlate client impact.

grace_eng: adding action items to backlog: `PROD-4281` (warmup automation), `PROD-4282` (circuit-breaker route), `PROD-4283` (tracing headers).

amy_cs: closing thread for now, will reopen if customer sees regressions. :thumbsup:
